solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dread holding the light thing

indicators.note: the word for dread holds the next word inside it, as a hand holds something

explanation.surface: Someone fearful clutching something weightless.
explanation.definitionFit: A plume from a bird is the classic example of something with almost no weight.

clue.text: Force with light weapons finally moves quickly

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of weapons

explanation.surface: An army with light arms finally manages to move fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letter of 'weapons'.
explanation.definitionFit: To flit is to dart or dash about swiftly and lightly, as a bird or bat does.

clue.text: Working doctor placing article as expected

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked over into a new shape

explanation.surface: A doctor at work positioning a piece of writing just as anticipated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges DOCTOR + PLACING + AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that go as expected have gone the way the scheme intended; the phrase is an idiom for that.

clue.text: Crowd tried to be heartless

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word for tried is dropped

parts.note: a case that is tried in court is heard

explanation.surface: A mob trying to be cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle A from HEARD; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group of people moving together, a mass or throng.

clue.text: Poke fun at director, embraced by friend in bawdy fashion

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them

indicators.note: embraced by puts the director's letter inside the word for friend

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Mocking a film director, hugged by a mate who jokes coarsely.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribald humour is coarse and rude, so acting this way is behaving in a crude, earthy manner.

clue.text: Soldiers look westward (it keeps the light off)

indicators.note: westward in an across clue means read from right to left

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Troops gaze west, with an aside about shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westward' turns LO into OL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade carried overhead blocks sunlight, which the bracketed phrase describes.

clue.text: Meeting nurse in a sort of jam

indicators.note: in places the nurse's letters within the fruit preserve

parts.note: plum is a kind of jam

explanation.surface: Meeting a nurse in a sticky situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of jam' reads as a predicament, but it is the fruit preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenum is a full assembly attended by all members, a type of gathering.

clue.text: Copies medical scan into answers

indicators.note: into says the scan goes inside the word for answers

parts.note: a CAT scan is computerised axial tomography

explanation.surface: A scan result slotted into a set of responses.
explanation.definitionFit: To replicate is to duplicate or reproduce, so the verb matches copies.

clue.text: Fuss over island's light entertainer

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first part sits above the second

parts.note: a song and dance is a fuss or commotion
the Isle of Man, often just Man

explanation.surface: A to-do over an island's comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaudeville performer who sings and dances provides light entertainment.

clue.text: Forming bubbles bursting near light

indicators.note: bursting suggests the letters of the two words break apart and regroup

explanation.surface: Bubbles bursting close to a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursting' rearranges NEAR + LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap that makes froth produces a foam of tiny bubbles, which is this verb.

clue.text: Blue car in crash can only get worse

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A blue car in a collision is a write-off that will only deteriorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges BLUE + CAR + IN; 'in' looks like a link but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition that cannot be cured or remedied will only deteriorate over time.

clue.text: Prize includes modish grape

indicators.note: includes means the prize word holds the fashionable word

parts.note: a pot is a trophy or prize

explanation.surface: A trophy featuring a trendy grape.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot is a family of wine grape varieties, such as Pinot Noir.

clue.text: Painful choice of direction

parts.note: S is the compass point south
E is the compass point east

explanation.surface: A hard decision about which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choice of direction' reads as S or E: two compass points with a choice between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tender or aching hurts, so it is a synonym of painful.

clue.text: One will carefully consider dropping resistance to light

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will

indicators.note: dropping says one letter is let fall from the combined words

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone who ponders, minus resistance, seeking enlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes R from I'LL RUMINATE; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To illuminate something is to shine a lamp on it, making it bright.

clue.text: A smash in 24 hours, fans begin supporting inexperienced rising star

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means sitting below the previous part
in puts the hit inside the day
rising in a down clue means read from the bottom up
begin asks for the opening letter of fans

explanation.surface: A hit record in a day, fans backing a new star on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: '24 hours' is a day, WED. 'rising' turns RAW into WAR; 'supporting' puts F, from 'fans begin', beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A white dwarf is a small dense stellar remnant, a specific kind of star.

clue.text: Not very cunning about window

indicators.note: about means the cunning word goes around the window word

parts.note: a light is a pane or window

explanation.surface: Something not very crafty concerning a window.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly means a little, to a small degree, which is a modest amount.

clue.text: Photographic technique cuts off so badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A photo method that crops images so poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges CUTS + OFF + SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately blurring an image slightly for a dreamy effect is a camera method.

clue.text: Film of Tensing and Hillary

indicators.note: of says the film is made of letters drawn from these names

explanation.surface: A movie about the Everest climbers Tenzing and Hillary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' signals the answer sits in 'tensinG AND HIllary'. The surface wants an Everest film; it is the 1982 Attenborough biopic.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Attenborough's 1982 biopic of the Indian independence leader is a famous movie.

clue.text: Possibly evening out near Lord Snooty?

parts.note: Lord Snooty, a Beano comic posh boy, is a toff, an upper-class person

explanation.surface: An outing with the posh comic character, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Snooty is a toff in the British comic The Beano; TOFF is slang for an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening free from work might be spent going out, so 'possibly' flags an example.

clue.text: Musical style of a tug in distress

indicators.note: in distress suggests the letters are in disarray

explanation.surface: A style of music depicting a tugboat in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' rearranges OF + A + TUG; 'of' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage in fugue-like style, with imitative counterpoint, is a musical manner.

clue.text: For openers, Farming Gazette features anger at supporter of compost burning

indicators.note: features means the paper's letters hold the next pieces
for openers asks for the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A farming paper carries a reader's angry letter about burning compost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter of compost' looks like one phrase; 'supporter' is the fan and 'of compost burning' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Firefang describes manure or compost scorched by overheating as it decomposes.

clue.text: Black Watch goes round wood

indicators.note: goes round says the watch word encircles the black letter

parts.note: a timer is a watch or clock
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The Black Watch regiment surrounds a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Watch is a Scottish army regiment. 'goes round' puts B inside TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber is wood used for building, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: It's very funny topping God in argument about source of brightness

indicators.note: about means the argument goes around everything else
in puts the shortened word inside the laughing letters

parts.note: LOL, laughing out loud, says something is very funny

indicators.note: topping means cutting off the head letter of the word God

parts.note: taken as written before losing its top

explanation.surface: A hilarious argument about outdoing God over light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' means beheading here, not beating; the shortened word sits inside the laughter, giving LOODL.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful lamp lighting a stadium or building is a source of illumination.

clue.text: Second vehicle one you probably shouldn't pick

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle, a taxi

explanation.surface: A second taxi is one you shouldn't choose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick' in the surface means choose; in the definition it means pick at a crust on a healing wound.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried crust over a healing wound should be left alone, not picked off.

clue.text: Male graduate says ichthyosaurs lacked heads

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts

indicators.note: heads asks for the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A male graduate claims prehistoric marine reptiles had no heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' takes S, I, L from 'says ichthyosaurs lacked'; 'lacked heads' looks like the instruction to behead.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a male given name, so it serves as an example of a man.

clue.text: Run away from cheat, avoiding city district

indicators.note: avoiding means the district's letters are left out

parts.note: to fleece someone is to swindle them
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Escape a swindler and steer clear of part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district of the City of London. 'avoiding' removes it from FLEECE.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee a place is to escape it in haste, a synonym of run away from.

clue.text: "Eyelashes" sounds less sensible

indicators.note: sounds means the word is said aloud

explanation.surface: A remark that lashes are more foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' signals CILIA is said like SILLIER, in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cilia is the anatomical term for lashes on the eyelid, as well as hair-like cell structures.

clue.text: Light in battery burners

indicators.note: in places the light inside the battery word

parts.note: a battery of punches is blows

explanation.surface: Lights in a battery-powered heater.
explanation.walkthrough: Battery means a beating, not a power cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowtorch sends a hot flame for brazing or paint stripping, so it is a burner.

clue.text: Unreliable friends have nothing for one to request

indicators.note: unreliable suggests the letters cannot be trusted to stay in order
for means one letter stands in for another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fickle mates have nothing to ask for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the I in FRIENDS for O, giving FROENDS; 'Unreliable' rearranges it. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon someone to come, as one does a doctor, is to ask for them.

clue.text: Discoverer of polarised light almost complimentary backing optical instrument

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off
backing means read in reverse

parts.note: a lens is an optical device

explanation.surface: A light pioneer, nearly free, supporting an optics device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims FREE to FRE; 'backing' turns LENS into SNEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustin-Jean Fresnel, the French physicist, did key work on light polarisation and waves.
